components.name: Recipe domain
components.responsibility: Own deterministic recipes, lookup, search, rails, and in-memory cookbook state.

components.name: Flask delivery layer
components.responsibility: Expose recipe APIs and choose mobile or TV presentation.

components.name: Mobile experience
components.responsibility: Render accessible browse, search, detail, and cookbook interactions.

components.name: TV experience
components.responsibility: Render ten-foot layouts and deterministic remote focus navigation.

components.name: Verification and documentation
components.responsibility: Prove domain behavior, terminology, accessibility-critical interactions, and startup instructions.

contracts.name: Recipe collection API
contracts.output: Recipe objects using the approved recipe schema
errors: Unknown recipe returns Recipe not found with HTTP 404

contracts.name: Cookbook API
contracts.input: Recipe ID for save or remove
errors: Unknown save returns a recipe-specific HTTP 400
Removing an absent recipe remains successful

contracts.name: Presentation mode contract
contracts.input: Request URL, mode query, user-agent hint, and recipe data
contracts.output: Mobile or TV semantic HTML preserving mode in navigation

contracts.name: Verification gate contract
contracts.output: Passing unit, browser, and terminology evidence
errors: Any required gate failure blocks completion

data_models.name: Recipe
invariants: Each recipe has at least three steps

data_models.name: Recipe rail
invariants: Non-cookbook rails contain at least two valid IDs

decisions.decision: Keep Flask, server-rendered HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
decisions.rationale: The PRD explicitly constrains the stack and offline workshop operation.

decisions.decision: Use one recipe-domain source of truth for API, mobile, and TV modes.
decisions.rationale: Shared data and search semantics prevent a partial rebrand and contract drift.

constraints: No frontend framework, database, build service, or external runtime dependency
The app works offline after dependencies are installed
Old movie and watchlist endpoints are removed
risks: Customer-visible terminology can remain in metadata or accessibility labels
Parallel UI changes can conflict in shared templates
TV focus can regress when rails have unequal lengths
